what_its_for: Pyridostigmine is used to treat myasthenia gravis, a condition that causes muscle weakness. It works by helping nerve signals reach your muscles more effectively, which improves muscle strength and reduces weakness. It may also be used for other conditions as directed by your doctor.
how_to_take: Take pyridostigmine exactly as your doctor prescribes. You can take it with or without food, but taking it with food or milk may help reduce stomach upset. Swallow extended-release tablets (Mestinon Timespan) whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. Regular tablets may be crushed if you have trouble swallowing. Try to take your doses at evenly spaced times throughout the day to keep the medicine working steadily in your body.
dosing: The dose your doctor prescribes will be based on your personal needs and how well your muscles are responding. A common starting dose for adults is 30 to 60 mg taken every 3 to 4 hours during waking hours. Extended-release tablets are usually taken once or twice a day, often at bedtime. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as your symptoms may get worse.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store pyridostigmine at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date printed on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking other medicines without checking with your doctor or pharmacist first, especially muscle relaxants, certain antibiotics (like gentamicin), heart medicines, or medicines for overactive bladder — these can interact with pyridostigmine. Avoid alcohol, as it may worsen side effects. Be careful driving or using machinery if you feel dizzy or weak. Try to avoid stress and extreme temperatures, as these can make myasthenia gravis symptoms worse.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: sudden or severe muscle weakness, trouble breathing or swallowing, chest tightness, very slow or fast heartbeat, severe nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea, excessive sweating or drooling, muscle cramps or twitching, blurred vision, or confusion. These could be signs of too much medication (cholinergic crisis) or worsening of your condition (myasthenic crisis), both of which need urgent medical attention.
when_it_works: Pyridostigmine usually starts working within 30 to 45 minutes after taking a regular tablet. Its effects typically last about 3 to 4 hours. You may notice improved muscle strength and less fatigue fairly quickly after starting treatment. Extended-release tablets take longer to start working but last longer. It is important to take your doses consistently as scheduled to maintain steady muscle strength throughout the day.
special_populations: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects and should be monitored closely. Pregnant women should only use this medicine if clearly needed — talk to your doctor, as pyridostigmine can pass to the baby. If you are breastfeeding, ask your doctor before using this medicine. People with asthma, kidney problems, heart rhythm problems, a history of seizures, or stomach/intestinal blockages should inform their doctor before starting this medication, as dose adjustments or extra monitoring may be needed.
